source_review.notes: Reviewed PostgreSQL 18 FSM and pg_freespacemap documentation plus the official PostgreSQL FSM implementation README, SQL Server page/extent/PFS documentation, Oracle Database 23 bitmap/ASSM concepts, MySQL 8.4 InnoDB physical-index documentation, and the two cited database-systems textbooks. All six online primary/official destinations returned HTTP 200. Precision, staleness, hint recovery, allocation, category, and ordered-index claims are scoped by engine.

evidence: Checked exact free f_i, quantum g, conservative q_i, max-tree nodes m_v, request r, upward threshold t, page capacity terms, and false-positive/negative terminology.
Checked exclusive separation of actual, advertised, immediately allocatable, reclaimable, page, extent, tablespace, file, and storage-pool space.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The upward-threshold model is deliberately conservative and is not PostgreSQL's exact request-encoding implementation.

evidence: Recomputed 16-byte encodings as 0,80,32,64,0,80,32,64 and root maximum 80.
Recomputed stale-high page 1 actual 60 and bucket 48, then page 5 insertion from 80 to 10/bucket zero.
Recomputed the 25-byte request selecting page 1, leaving actual 35 and bucket 32.
Recomputed stale-low page 7 actual 80 versus bucket 64, no 70-byte candidate before repair, and page 7 after repair.
Recomputed 32-byte exercise buckets, errors, tree parents, and bubble-up update.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No vendor precision, retry rate, tree shape, or production capacity is inferred.

evidence: Re-derived q_i=g*floor(f_i/g) and q_i<=f_i<q_i+g.
Re-derived upward request threshold g*ceil(r/g) and its conservative guarantee plus marginal false negatives.
Re-derived internal maxima and the root/no-candidate implication by induction.
Re-derived leaf update propagation until a parent maximum remains unchanged or root is reached.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The tree proof covers summary values in one snapshot, not page identity, actual current space, or concurrent insertion.

evidence: Reviewed zero/full/exact-fit pages, slot limit despite bytes, every bucket boundary, saturation, partial/non-power-of-two trees, and invalid topology/parent values.
Reviewed stale-high/low leaves, concurrent consumption/cleanup, hot candidates, retry storms, missing feedback, bounded progress, and lock-order deadlock.
Reviewed dead-but-visible tuples, undo/recovery retention, fragmented-but-not-contiguous bytes, compression uncertainty, and deliberate fill headroom.
Reviewed relation extension/truncation/generation change, entries beyond durable size, map loss/torn parent/leaf, checksum failure, full disk, backup/restore, and safe rebuild.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Repair derives summaries only from authenticated currently owned data pages and never treats an unreadable page as free.

evidence: Validated every model leaf is a conservative multiple of 16 at its update time.
Validated all internal tree nodes equal the maximum of their children after construction and updates.
Validated left-first search reaches a qualifying represented leaf or returns none when root is below threshold.
Validated stale-high correction, data-page recheck, stale-low repair, and exact ten-line stdout with empty stderr/zero exit.
invariant_checking.notes: The model omits primary page bytes, ownership, cleanup eligibility, slots, latches, WAL, checksums, contention, and crash recovery.

evidence: Reviewed floor-quantization bounds and upward-threshold candidate guarantee.
Reviewed the max-tree descent invariant from root to leaf.
Reviewed bubble-up correctness from updated leaf to root.
Reviewed counterexamples showing stale summaries and quantization cannot authorize actual insertion.
proof_review.notes: No universal search policy, logging strategy, concurrency progress, or repair correctness proof is claimed.

evidence: Separated summary candidate discovery from data-page authority and page capacity from page/extent ownership.
Separated safe hint staleness from corruption of correctness-critical allocation metadata.
Separated allocatable, reclaimable, internally reusable, and operating-system-released space.
Labeled the model's encoding/search conventions and non-vendor scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Exact, free, safe, authoritative, logged, recoverable, corrupt, and repaired claims name their layer and premises.

evidence: The standard-library free-space max-tree lifecycle executed successfully through the repository verifier.
All six online primary/official destinations returned HTTP 200 on 2026-08-30.
Front matter, exact section order, local links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippet expectations passed draft validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live FSM/PFS/ASSM/allocation map, data page, concurrent allocator, WAL recovery, corruption repair, relation extension, crash, backup/restore, or workload was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently treats free-space metadata as a representation/search/repair layer whose authority and failure semantics must be distinguished from actual data pages and allocation ownership.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed exact page fit, maps/trees/bitmaps/lists, quantization, selection, retry, staleness, visibility/reclamation, eager/lazy updates, logging authority, crash states, repair, monitoring, contention, extension, and capacity layers.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, executable max-tree lifecycle, ten distinct algorithm/concurrency/recovery examples, and five progressive exercises support self-study from bucket arithmetic through production growth diagnosis.

limitations: Internal authoring, official/primary-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model do not certify PostgreSQL FSM, SQL Server PFS/allocation maps, Oracle ASSM, InnoDB, or any live map/page, logging policy, allocation ownership, concurrency progress, repair, crash recovery, capacity, workload result, or production fitness.
